question_or_symptom: The root ignore policy rejected the new authored repository when the coordinator attempted to stage it as a gitlink.
observation: Forcing the add would bypass the same policy intended to prevent source trees, build products, models, and environments from entering the coordinator history. A narrow path exception still allows the hook and resume verifier to require mode 160000.
conclusion: A registered gitlink should be authorized declaratively, not smuggled through an ignore rule with a force option.
decision: Add an exact .gitignore exception for each project-authored lane, use ordinary git add, and retain the staged/tracked policy gates that reject any projects entry that is not a mode-160000 gitlink.
invalidated_assumptions: Using git add -f for a known gitlink is equivalent to an auditable, tracked exception in the repository policy.
